top_strength: Joel gave a genuinely honest explanation of why the hourly rate exists — walking distance, shared elevators at the destination, and the risk of the crew not getting everything unloaded — instead of overpromising to close a rushed same-day-ish booking. He also explained the arrival-window mechanics clearly (morning move first, crew calls ahead with a heads-up), which is the FAQ this customer most needed answered.
coaching_note: This call closed on price alone and skipped every differentiator — No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and no hidden fees were all absent, and so was the entire Save Your Ass prep speech even after the customer said he could move his own boxes. The single highest-value fix: this customer's mover bailed 30 minutes earlier and his only real concern was the 1:30-4:00 elevator reservation, which Joel answered three times with 'okay, sounds good' without ever resolving it or offering the On-Time Guarantee. Slow down, acknowledge the stressor out loud, and run the full pricing block — a stressed customer who already said '$505, that's perfect' was the easiest audience in the world for the value pitch.
